knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(scrutiny)
```

Consistency tests, such as GRIM, check whether two or more summary values can describe the same data. To implement a new one with scrutiny, write the core logic of the test and let scrutiny's function factories apply it to data frames. This vignette shows the minimal steps; for details, see `vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth")`.

## 1. Single-case

Write the test as a function that takes single values and returns `TRUE` if they are consistent, `FALSE` if they are not, and `NA` if the case can't be decided. End its name in `_scalar`. Here, the test is a mock one without real meaning, called SCHLIM:

```{r}
schlim_scalar <- function(y, n) {
  (y / 3) > n
}

schlim_scalar(y = 30, n = 4)
schlim_scalar(y = 2, n = 7)
```

## 2. Vectorized

`Vectorize()` turns the single-case function into one whose arguments can have a length greater than 1:

```{r}
schlim <- Vectorize(schlim_scalar)

schlim(y = 10:15, n = 4)
```

This works if every argument of the single-case function is a value to be tested and the function always returns a single value. Otherwise, write the signature out; see `vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth")`.

## 3. Basic mapper

`function_map()` creates a function that tests every row of a data frame, like `grim_map()`. End its name in `_map`:

```{r}
schlim_map <- function_map(
  .fun = schlim_scalar,
  .reported = c("y", "n"),
  .name_test = "SCHLIM"
)

# Example data:
df1 <- tibble::tibble(y = 16:25, n = 3:12)

schlim_map(df1)
```

## 4. `audit()` method

For summaries with `audit()`, write a method named `audit.scrutiny_<name>_map()`, where `<name>` is the test's `.name_test` in lowercase, here `schlim`. Call `audit_cols_minimal()` in its body:

```{r}
audit.scrutiny_schlim_map <- function(data, ...) {
  audit_cols_minimal(data)
}

df1 |>
  schlim_map() |>
  audit()
```

`audit_cols_minimal()` only provides the most basic summaries. You can add statistics specific to your test; for an example, see the *Summaries with `audit()`* section of `?grim_map`.

## 5. Sequence mapper

A sequence mapper tests values around the reported ones, like `grim_map_seq()`. `function_map_seq()` creates it from the basic mapper:

```{r}
schlim_map_seq <- function_map_seq(
  .fun = schlim_map,
  .reported = c("y", "n"),
  .name_test = "SCHLIM"
)

df1 |>
  schlim_map_seq()
```

Get summary statistics with `audit_seq()`:

```{r}
df1 |>
  schlim_map_seq() |>
  audit_seq()
```

## 6. Total-n mapper

Suppose two groups are reported with their values but only a total sample size:

```{r}
df2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~y1, ~y2, ~n,
   84,  37,  29,
   61,  55,  26
)
```

A total-n mapper tests hypothetical group sizes, like `grim_map_total_n()`:

```{r}
schlim_map_total_n <- function_map_total_n(
  .fun = schlim_map,
  .reported = "y",
  .name_test = "SCHLIM"
)

df2 |>
  schlim_map_total_n()
```

Get summary statistics with `audit_total_n()`:

```{r}
df2 |>
  schlim_map_total_n() |>
  audit_total_n()
```
